TurboRegs replaces this fragmented process with a structured, intelligent system that brings speed, accuracy, and transparency to regulatory readiness.

The platform digitizes regulatory intake, document collection, and submission workflows while enforcing completeness and consistency across studies. Using AI, TurboRegs identifies missing or outdated documents, validates required elements, and ensures submissions are IRB-ready the first time.

With TurboRegs, sponsors, CROs, and research sites can:
• Standardize regulatory packets across studies and investigators
• Reduce back-and-forth caused by incomplete submissions
• Gain real-time visibility into submission status and readiness
• Maintain a centralized, audit-ready regulatory document source
• Scale regulatory operations across portfolios and site networks

Rather than serving as another eReg repository, TurboRegs acts as a regulatory orchestration engine—turning regulatory data into structured assets and workflows that keep studies moving.

TurboRegs sets the regulatory cadence of clinical trials—eliminating startup drag and accelerating IRB readiness.

entity.name: DnXT Solutions
entity.description:
DNXT Solutions is a software and consulting company focused on regulatory operations for life sciences.

Our platform — DNXT Publisher Suite — handles eCTD submission assembly, document validation, and regulatory publishing for Pharma, biotech, and CRO organizations. From dossier planning to agency submission, teams use a single platform instead of stitching together manual processes and legacy tools.

Our consulting team brings hands-on experience in regulatory operations, system implementation, and end-to-end delivery across R&D and commercial functions. We work with organizations to assess, optimize, and modernize their regulatory technology and processes.

 What we focus on:

 - AI-Assisted Document Preparation: Automated link creation, bookmark generation, and cross-reference validation to reduce the manual work that often leads to technical deficiencies.

 - Multi-Regional Support: Publish to FDA, EMA, Health Canada, TGA, and other agencies from one platform. eCTD 3.x and 4.0 supported.

 - Compliance & Security: 21 CFR Part 11 compliant. Full audit trail on every action.

 - CRO-Ready Architecture: Multi-tenant design with data isolation so CROs can manage multiple sponsors from a single instance.

 - Consulting Services: Regulatory operations strategy, system implementation, process optimization, and technology advisory for life sciences organizations.

Our customers have seen meaningful improvements in submission prep time, first-time acceptance rates, and audit readiness. Implementation typically takes 4-12 weeks.

We integrate with Veeva Vault, SharePoint, Box, Documentum, Okta, Azure AD, and other systems commonly used in regulatory workflows.

 Learn more: https://www.dnxtsolutions.com

entity.name: TurboRegs
entity.description:
TurboRegs is an AI-driven regulatory workflow platform designed to accelerate clinical trial startup by simplifying and standardizing regulatory submissions.

Regulatory packets are still assembled manually across emails, shared drives, and disconnected documents—creating rework, version confusion, and avoidable delays at the IRB and site level. TurboRegs replaces this fragmented process with a structured, intelligent system that brings speed, accuracy, and transparency to regulatory readiness.

The platform digitizes regulatory intake, document collection, and submission workflows while enforcing completeness and consistency across studies. Using AI, TurboRegs identifies missing or outdated documents, validates required elements, and ensures submissions are IRB-ready the first time.

With TurboRegs, sponsors, CROs, and research sites can:
• Standardize regulatory packets across studies and investigators
• Reduce back-and-forth caused by incomplete submissions
• Gain real-time visibility into submission status and readiness
• Maintain a centralized, audit-ready regulatory document source
• Scale regulatory operations across portfolios and site networks

Rather than serving as another eReg repository, TurboRegs acts as a regulatory orchestration engine—turning regulatory data into structured assets and workflows that keep studies moving.

TurboRegs sets the regulatory cadence of clinical trials—eliminating startup drag and accelerating IRB readiness.

entity.name: TurboRegs
entity.description:
TurboRegs is an AI-driven regulatory workflow platform designed to accelerate clinical trial startup by simplifying and standardizing regulatory submissions.

Regulatory packets are still assembled manually across emails, shared drives, and disconnected documents—creating rework, version confusion, and avoidable delays at the IRB and site level. TurboRegs replaces this fragmented process with a structured, intelligent system that brings speed, accuracy, and transparency to regulatory readiness.

The platform digitizes regulatory intake, document collection, and submission workflows while enforcing completeness and consistency across studies. Using AI, TurboRegs identifies missing or outdated documents, validates required elements, and ensures submissions are IRB-ready the first time.

With TurboRegs, sponsors, CROs, and research sites can:
• Standardize regulatory packets across studies and investigators
• Reduce back-and-forth caused by incomplete submissions
• Gain real-time visibility into submission status and readiness
• Maintain a centralized, audit-ready regulatory document source
• Scale regulatory operations across portfolios and site networks

Rather than serving as another eReg repository, TurboRegs acts as a regulatory orchestration engine—turning regulatory data into structured assets and workflows that keep studies moving.

TurboRegs sets the regulatory cadence of clinical trials—eliminating startup drag and accelerating IRB readiness.

You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

Examples:
  - HubSpot ↔ a smaller CRM/marketing-automation platform: true.
  - HubSpot ↔ a lead-generation agency using HubSpot for clients: false.
  - Shopify ↔ an online-store/e-commerce platform: true.
  - Shopify ↔ a payment processor with no storefront platform: false.
  - Grab ↔ a ride-hailing marketplace: true.
  - Grab ↔ a traditional car-rental operator with no on-demand marketplace: false.
  - Rippling ↔ a smaller HRIS/payroll platform: true.
  - Rippling ↔ device-security software for mobile workers: false.
  - Brex ↔ a corporate-card and spend-management platform: true.
  - Brex ↔ consumer personal-finance budgeting software: false.
  - OpenAI ↔ a foundation-model/API company: true.
  - OpenAI ↔ a consultancy that implements AI tools for clients: false.
  - Datadog ↔ an application-performance-monitoring and observability platform: true.
  - Datadog ↔ a generic IT consulting firm: false.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ an endpoint-security platform: true.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ a general-purpose IT monitoring tool with no security product: false.
  - Procore ↔ construction project-management software: true.
  - Procore ↔ a construction contractor: false.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ field-service management software for trades businesses: true.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ a plumbing company that uses field-service software: false.
  - Teladoc ↔ a virtual-care/telehealth platform: true.
  - Teladoc ↔ a health-insurance carrier with no telehealth product: false.
  - Veeva ↔ life-sciences CRM or clinical-operations software: true.
  - Veeva ↔ a generic CRM with no life-sciences focus: false.

SEED:
  name: Veeva
  domain: veeva.com
  description: Cloud software for life sciences companies, including CRM, clinical, regulatory, quality, and content operations

CANDIDATE:
  name: BSI Life Sciences
  description: CTMS, eTMF and beyond: Empower your clinical teams with user-friendly, compliant, and cost-efficient solutions.

We make eClinical software that helps life sciences companies manage their clinical development processes securely and in full compliance with an integrated CTMS and eTMF that connects directly with leading EDC solutions for a single, connected platform for clinical operations.

properties.name: CMC Regulatory Services, LLC
properties.description:
CMC Regulatory Services, LLC is a specialized CMC and Regulatory Affairs consultancy dedicated to helping biopharmaceutical companies transform complex science into successful regulatory submissions.

For more than three decades, we have supported sponsors across all stages of development—from early IND-enabling programs through NDA and BLA approvals. Our core focus is Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls (CMC), with deep expertise in authoring, editing, and strategically structuring FDA-ready Module 3 submissions.

We provide both hands-on technical execution and high-level regulatory strategy. Whether a company needs targeted authorship of specific sections, complete Module 3 development, lifecycle management support, or strategic guidance in response to FDA feedback, we deliver practical, risk-based solutions grounded in regulatory science.

Our experience spans small emerging biotechs to established global pharmaceutical companies. We have worked across diverse therapeutic modalities, including complex biologics, therapeutic proteins, cell and gene therapies, and combination products. In addition to de novo submission development, we frequently assist clients in resolving CMC deficiencies, addressing Complete Response Letters, and rescuing challenged regulatory programs.

We are known for precision, clarity, and disciplined document architecture. Our approach emphasizes proactive communication with Health Authorities, alignment with current FDA expectations, and meticulous attention to detail to prevent costly delays.

At our core, we help companies overcome regulatory CMC challenges through thoughtful strategy, technical rigor, and innovative problem-solving.

You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

Examples:
  - HubSpot ↔ a smaller CRM/marketing-automation platform: true.
  - HubSpot ↔ a lead-generation agency using HubSpot for clients: false.
  - Shopify ↔ an online-store/e-commerce platform: true.
  - Shopify ↔ a payment processor with no storefront platform: false.
  - Grab ↔ a ride-hailing marketplace: true.
  - Grab ↔ a traditional car-rental operator with no on-demand marketplace: false.
  - Rippling ↔ a smaller HRIS/payroll platform: true.
  - Rippling ↔ device-security software for mobile workers: false.
  - Brex ↔ a corporate-card and spend-management platform: true.
  - Brex ↔ consumer personal-finance budgeting software: false.
  - OpenAI ↔ a foundation-model/API company: true.
  - OpenAI ↔ a consultancy that implements AI tools for clients: false.

  - Datadog ↔ a generic IT consulting firm: false.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ an endpoint-security platform: true.

  - Procore ↔ a construction contractor: false.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ field-service management software for trades businesses: true.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ a plumbing company that uses field-service software: false.
  - Teladoc ↔ a virtual-care/telehealth platform: true.
  - Teladoc ↔ a health-insurance carrier with no telehealth product: false.
  - Veeva ↔ life-sciences CRM or clinical-operations software: true.
  - Veeva ↔ a generic CRM with no life-sciences focus: false.
